name: DTFSeeds Education Visual Production Queue — Harvest/Post-Harvest + Outdoor
purpose: Asset-level production plan for the next educational visual wave. It extends the canonical coverage targets without changing the existing publication boundary or placement rules.

designSystem.style: academic studio-quality cultivation education; clean neutral/cream background; natural plant color; crisp labels; no yellow cast; no decorative clutter
designSystem.textPolicy: Keep baked-in text concise. Prefer diagram labels, short callouts, legends, and captions over paragraph text.
designSystem.accuracyPolicy: No unsupported universal thresholds. Numeric targets must be source-supported and context-labeled. Diagnostic visuals must distinguish observation from interpretation.
designSystem.accessibilityPolicy: Every asset requires descriptive alt text and a caption that communicates the educational point without relying on color alone.
designSystem.reviewPolicy: Artwork remains artwork-needed until visual QA, scientific QA, spelling/label QA, and page-placement QA are all complete.

items.title: Harvest Readiness: Multiple Signals, Not One
items.educationalPurpose: Compare flower maturity signals across pistils, calyx swelling, trichomes, plant fade, and whole-plant context without presenting any single sign as decisive.
items.altText: Compare flower maturity signals across pistils, calyx swelling, trichomes, plant fade, and whole-plant context without presenting any single sign as decisive.
items.caption: Harvest readiness is assessed from multiple plant signals together; no single visual cue should be treated as a universal trigger.

items.title: Trichome Maturity Under Magnification
items.educationalPurpose: Show clear, cloudy, and amber glandular trichome appearances under consistent magnification, with a caution that lighting and camera white balance can distort interpretation.
items.altText: Show clear, cloudy, and amber glandular trichome appearances under consistent magnification, with a caution that lighting and camera white balance can distort interpretation.
items.caption: Trichome appearance can help assess maturation when viewed under consistent magnification and lighting.

items.title: Harvest Handling Workflow
items.educationalPurpose: Illustrate a clean sequence from pre-harvest setup through cutting, transport, trimming strategy, and entry into drying while minimizing unnecessary handling.
items.altText: Illustrate a clean sequence from pre-harvest setup through cutting, transport, trimming strategy, and entry into drying while minimizing unnecessary handling.
items.caption: A clean harvest workflow reduces handling damage and moves flowers efficiently into controlled drying.

items.title: Bud Washing: What It Is and When It Is Considered
items.educationalPurpose: Explain bud washing as a post-harvest rinse concept, distinguish it from remediation, and show decision factors such as outdoor debris, dust, and visible contamination concerns.
items.altText: Explain bud washing as a post-harvest rinse concept, distinguish it from remediation, and show decision factors such as outdoor debris, dust, and visible contamination concerns.
items.caption: Bud washing is a post-harvest rinsing practice sometimes used to remove surface debris; it is not a substitute for contamination prevention.

items.title: Drying Environment Fundamentals
items.educationalPurpose: Visualize temperature, relative humidity, air exchange, gentle circulation, darkness, hanging density, and monitoring as interacting variables rather than isolated targets.
items.altText: Visualize temperature, relative humidity, air exchange, gentle circulation, darkness, hanging density, and monitoring as interacting variables rather than isolated targets.
items.caption: Controlled drying depends on stable temperature, humidity, airflow, darkness, spacing, and monitoring.

items.title: Drying Failure Modes
items.educationalPurpose: Compare overdrying, uneven drying, stalled drying, excessive direct airflow, and mold-risk conditions with observable warning signs and corrective monitoring priorities.
items.altText: Compare overdrying, uneven drying, stalled drying, excessive direct airflow, and mold-risk conditions with observable warning signs and corrective monitoring priorities.
items.caption: Drying problems can often be traced to unstable humidity, excessive airflow, poor spacing, or overly rapid moisture loss.

items.title: Water Activity: Moisture Availability vs. Moisture Content
items.educationalPurpose: Explain water activity as available water rather than total water content, show why the distinction matters for storage stability, and avoid unsupported universal pass/fail claims.
items.altText: Explain water activity as available water rather than total water content, show why the distinction matters for storage stability, and avoid unsupported universal pass/fail claims.
items.caption: Water activity describes how available water is for physical, chemical, and microbial processes; it is different from total moisture content.

items.title: Curing Workflow and Moisture Equalization
items.educationalPurpose: Illustrate stabilization after drying, container loading, observation, periodic checks, moisture equalization, and storage transition without presenting curing as a way to fix unsafe material.
items.altText: Illustrate stabilization after drying, container loading, observation, periodic checks, moisture equalization, and storage transition without presenting curing as a way to fix unsafe material.
items.caption: Curing is a controlled post-drying stabilization process that depends on properly dried material and ongoing observation.

items.title: Storage Environment: Light, Heat, Oxygen and Moisture
items.educationalPurpose: Show how light, elevated heat, excess oxygen exposure, and unsuitable moisture conditions can accelerate quality loss during storage.
items.altText: Show how light, elevated heat, excess oxygen exposure, and unsuitable moisture conditions can accelerate quality loss during storage.
items.caption: Stable, dark, moderate storage conditions help limit quality degradation driven by light, heat, oxygen, and moisture.

items.requiredTopic: light oxygen heat and moisture degradation
items.title: Post-Harvest Degradation Pathways
items.educationalPurpose: Map major post-harvest stressors to likely quality consequences such as oxidation, aroma loss, color changes, texture changes, and microbial risk.
items.altText: Map major post-harvest stressors to likely quality consequences such as oxidation, aroma loss, color changes, texture changes, and microbial risk.
items.caption: Post-harvest quality can decline through interacting light, oxygen, heat, and moisture pathways.

items.title: Outdoor Site Selection
items.educationalPurpose: Evaluate direct sun exposure, drainage, air movement, access to water, privacy/security constraints, slope, soil/media plan, and nearby contamination or pollen sources.
items.altText: Evaluate direct sun exposure, drainage, air movement, access to water, privacy/security constraints, slope, soil/media plan, and nearby contamination or pollen sources.
items.caption: Outdoor site selection should consider sun, drainage, airflow, water access, terrain, and nearby biological or environmental risks.

items.title: Sun Path and Seasonal Exposure
items.educationalPurpose: Illustrate changing solar angle and day length across a season and how buildings, trees, and terrain create moving shade.
items.altText: Illustrate changing solar angle and day length across a season and how buildings, trees, and terrain create moving shade.
items.caption: Seasonal sun angle, day length, and surrounding obstacles determine how much direct light an outdoor crop actually receives.

items.title: Hardening Off: Indoor to Outdoor Transition
items.educationalPurpose: Show gradual exposure to brighter light, wind, temperature variation, and outdoor humidity while monitoring stress response.
items.altText: Show gradual exposure to brighter light, wind, temperature variation, and outdoor humidity while monitoring stress response.
items.caption: Hardening off gradually acclimates plants to outdoor light, wind, and temperature variability.

items.title: Outdoor Transplanting and Root Establishment
items.educationalPurpose: Illustrate transplant timing considerations, root-ball handling, planting depth, immediate watering, temporary support, mulch clearance at the stem, and early establishment monitoring.
items.altText: Illustrate transplant timing considerations, root-ball handling, planting depth, immediate watering, temporary support, mulch clearance at the stem, and early establishment monitoring.
items.caption: Successful outdoor transplanting depends on careful root handling, stable placement, irrigation, and early establishment monitoring.

items.title: Wind Load and Structural Support
items.educationalPurpose: Show prevailing wind, leverage on branches, staking/trellising options, flexible ties, and why support should distribute load without girdling stems.
items.altText: Show prevailing wind, leverage on branches, staking/trellising options, flexible ties, and why support should distribute load without girdling stems.
items.caption: Outdoor support systems should reduce wind leverage while allowing normal stem movement and avoiding constriction.

items.title: Rain, Dense Flowers and Moisture Risk
items.educationalPurpose: Visualize how repeated rain, dense floral structure, cool nights, poor airflow, and trapped moisture can combine to elevate disease risk late in the season.
items.altText: Visualize how repeated rain, dense floral structure, cool nights, poor airflow, and trapped moisture can combine to elevate disease risk late in the season.
items.caption: Persistent moisture around dense flowers can increase disease risk, especially when airflow and drying conditions are limited.

items.title: Outdoor Irrigation: Root-Zone Coverage and Timing
items.educationalPurpose: Compare shallow frequent wetting with deeper root-zone irrigation, show emitter placement and runoff/drainage considerations, and emphasize observation-based adjustment.
items.altText: Compare shallow frequent wetting with deeper root-zone irrigation, show emitter placement and runoff/drainage considerations, and emphasize observation-based adjustment.
items.caption: Outdoor irrigation should wet the active root zone evenly while accounting for weather, drainage, container or soil volume, and plant demand.

items.title: Wildlife Protection by Exclusion
items.educationalPurpose: Illustrate fencing, trunk guards, netting where appropriate, sanitation, and site design as prevention-first strategies without harmful trapping instructions.
items.altText: Illustrate fencing, trunk guards, netting where appropriate, sanitation, and site design as prevention-first strategies without harmful trapping instructions.
items.caption: Physical exclusion and site design are preferred first-line approaches for reducing wildlife damage.

items.title: Outdoor Microclimates Around the Plant
items.educationalPurpose: Show how slope, walls, ground cover, shade, windbreaks, canopy density, and nearby water or structures alter temperature, humidity, wind, and drying rate.
items.altText: Show how slope, walls, ground cover, shade, windbreaks, canopy density, and nearby water or structures alter temperature, humidity, wind, and drying rate.
items.caption: Small differences in terrain and surrounding structures can create meaningful microclimates around outdoor plants.

items.title: Pollen Drift and Unwanted Pollination Risk
items.educationalPurpose: Explain airborne pollen movement, directionality with wind, uncertainty in travel distance, and why geographic separation alone cannot guarantee isolation.
items.altText: Explain airborne pollen movement, directionality with wind, uncertainty in travel distance, and why geographic separation alone cannot guarantee isolation.
items.caption: Airborne pollen can move with wind, so unwanted pollination risk depends on source presence, wind, timing, and local terrain.

items.title: Outdoor Seasonal Planning Timeline
items.educationalPurpose: Organize site preparation, acclimation, transplanting, vegetative growth, reproductive transition, weather-risk periods, harvest monitoring, and post-season sanitation on a flexible seasonal timeline.
items.altText: Organize site preparation, acclimation, transplanting, vegetative growth, reproductive transition, weather-risk periods, harvest monitoring, and post-season sanitation on a flexible seasonal timeline.
items.caption: Outdoor planning works best as a flexible seasonal timeline tied to local weather, day length, and plant development.
